title: Sense of Life
summary: A sense of life as a pre-conceptual, emotional appraisal of man and of existence.

lessons.title: What the phrase names
lessons.objective: Name a sense of life as a pre-conceptual, emotional appraisal, and reject the usual substitutes.

exercises.prompt: What is a sense of life?

choices.text: A pre-conceptual, emotional appraisal of man and of existence
A finished system of explicit philosophy
A proof that discovers facts by feeling
A passing mood about one event

feedback.note: The unit names one thing: a sense of life is a pre-conceptual, emotional appraisal of man and of existence.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the definition to what it stresses.

pairs.right: Felt as an appraisal, not argued as a proof
A judgment, not a blank reaction

feedback.note: Each word does a job. The appraisal comes before a stated philosophy, it is felt, and it judges.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition.

parts.text: A sense of life is a pre-conceptual, emotional

feedback.note: The noun in the definition is appraisal. A sense of life judges; it does not prove, tally, or drift.

exercises.prompt: Which word says the appraisal is felt rather than argued?

choices.text: Emotional
Pre-conceptual
Of man
Of existence

feedback.note: Emotional names the form of the appraisal. The other phrases name its timing or its objects.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition in order.

feedback.note: Keep the whole phrase together. A sense of life is not a laboratory result standing in for that appraisal.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence stays inside this unit?

choices.text: A sense of life is how one emotionally appraises man and existence before stating a philosophy.
A sense of life is a scientific instrument.
A sense of life is a political party.
A sense of life is only a taste in furniture.

feedback.note: Stay with the definition. Instruments, parties, and furniture tastes are different subjects.

exercises.prompt: Match each substitute to why it misses the definition.

pairs.right: Too narrow to be an appraisal of man and existence

feedback.note: A sense of life is earlier than a stated philosophy, emotional rather than a proof, and aimed at man and existence rather than one incident.

exercises.prompt: Name the two traits of the appraisal.

feedback.note: The two traits are pre-conceptual and emotional. The definition does not call a sense of life innate or statistical.

lessons.title: An appraisal of man
lessons.objective: Identify man as one object of the appraisal: what kind of being one takes a human being to be.

exercises.prompt: One object of a sense of life is man. What does that object cover?

choices.text: What kind of being one takes a human being to be
Whether one bus was late today
Which color one prefers on a wall
Which tax rate was passed this year

feedback.note: Appraising man means an emotional estimate of human beings as such, not a reaction to one errand, color, or statute.

exercises.prompt: Build the question an appraisal of man asks.

feedback.note: The object man raises a question about the kind of being a human is. A chair or a late bus is not that question.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its role.

pairs.right: One object of a sense of life

feedback.note: Man, in this definition, is the human being as such. One irritation does not stand in for that appraisal.

exercises.prompt: Which line is an appraisal of man?

choices.text: People are the kind of beings who can choose and achieve.
I am annoyed that the bus was late.
The sky looks blue this afternoon.
This chair is made of wood.

feedback.note: An appraisal of man estimates the kind of being a person is. Weather, wood, and one delay are not that estimate.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the object.

parts.text: A sense of life includes an emotional appraisal of

feedback.note: The definition names man as an object. Furniture, weather, and ballots are outside that object.

exercises.prompt: A harsh appraisal of man would be an emotional estimate that human beings are, by nature,

choices.text: Helpless or corrupt
Five minutes late to one meeting
Taller than a doorway
Paid in a particular currency

feedback.note: An appraisal of man judges the kind of being people are. Height, pay, and one delay are not that judgment.

exercises.prompt: Match each emotional estimate of man to the view it expresses.

pairs.left: People can be efficacious and worthy
People are corrupt or helpless by nature

feedback.note: Opposite appraisals of man still appraise man. A dislike of one delay does not.

exercises.prompt: If a definition of sense of life dropped man, what would be lost?

choices.text: One of the two objects the appraisal is about
Its power to prove facts
Nothing, because the definition would then be complete
Its status as a full philosophy course

feedback.note: Man is one of the two objects. Dropping it leaves the appraisal incomplete. It never was a proof or a course.

lessons.title: An appraisal of existence
lessons.objective: Identify existence as the other object: an emotional estimate of the world a human being faces.

exercises.prompt: Match each object to the question it raises.

pairs.right: What kind of being a human is
What the world is like for a human being
The full object of a sense of life

feedback.note: A sense of life appraises man and existence together. Each object asks its own question.

exercises.prompt: Besides man, what does a sense of life appraise?

choices.text: Existence
Today’s menu
One game’s score
The price of one ticket

feedback.note: The second object is existence, the world as such, not a menu, a score, or a ticket price.

exercises.prompt: Complete the pair of objects.

parts.text: A sense of life is an emotional appraisal of man and of

feedback.note: The pair is man and existence. Headlines, fashions, and schedules are not the second object.

exercises.prompt: Build what an appraisal of existence estimates.

feedback.note: Existence here means the world a human being faces, not one day’s forecast standing alone.

exercises.prompt: Which line appraises existence rather than one event?

choices.text: The world is the kind of place in which a human being can live and succeed.
It is raining on this street right now.
The train was late once.
This cup is empty.

feedback.note: An appraisal of existence estimates the world as such. Rain, a delay, and an empty cup are single facts, not that estimate.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the scale it belongs to.

feedback.note: Keep the scale. Existence is the world as such, and the sense of life is a judgment about it, not a report of one storm.

exercises.prompt: A sense of life that appraised only man, and never existence, would be

choices.text: Incomplete, because existence is the other object
Complete, because man is the only object
A proof about the weather
An explicit philosophy course

feedback.note: The definition names two objects. Leaving out existence leaves the appraisal unfinished.

exercises.prompt: State both objects.

feedback.note: Both objects belong in the definition: man and existence. Fashion and traffic do not replace them.

lessons.title: Before a stated philosophy
lessons.objective: Hold that the appraisal is in place before it is translated into explicit ideas, without treating the feeling as a proof.

exercises.prompt: What does pre-conceptual say about a sense of life?

choices.text: The appraisal is held before it is stated as an explicit philosophy
The appraisal has no view of man or existence
The appraisal is inherited as a gene
The appraisal can never be put into concepts later

feedback.note: Pre-conceptual means before a stated philosophy. It does not mean empty, genetic, or forever wordless.

exercises.prompt: Place a sense of life relative to philosophy.

feedback.note: The timing word is before. A sense of life is not a substitute for philosophy and it is not itself a proof.

exercises.prompt: Match each term to its place.

pairs.right: The emotional appraisal, before it is stated
The word that marks that order

feedback.note: A sense of life and an explicit philosophy are different forms. Pre-conceptual marks which one comes first.

exercises.prompt: Which mistake treats a sense of life as already a philosophy?

choices.text: Calling the feeling a finished system of ideas
Saying the appraisal comes before a stated system
Saying it appraises both man and existence
Saying the appraisal is emotional

feedback.note: A finished system of ideas is a philosophy. A sense of life is the earlier, emotional appraisal, not that system.

exercises.prompt: Build the order this unit uses.

feedback.note: The order is sense of life, then an explicit philosophy. The feeling does not replace thinking or prove the facts.

exercises.prompt: Someone feels that the world is closed against human effort, but has never stated a philosophy. What do they have, on this unit’s terms?

choices.text: A sense of life: a pre-conceptual emotional appraisal
A completed philosophy course
A proof that the world is closed
Nothing, because only stated ideas count

feedback.note: An unstated emotional estimate of man and existence is already a sense of life. It is not yet a philosophy, and it is not a proof.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the verdict.

pairs.left: It is not yet stated in concepts
It still judges man and existence
pairs.right: That is why it is an appraisal
That claim does not belong in this unit

feedback.note: Pre-conceptual still leaves an appraisal with objects. It does not turn emotion into a way of proving facts.

exercises.prompt: Why can a sense of life and a philosophy disagree in a person’s life?

choices.text: One is an emotional appraisal and the other is a set of explicit ideas
They are the same thing under two names
The feeling has already proved which ideas are true
A sense of life has no content that ideas could match

feedback.note: They are different forms of appraisal, emotional and conceptual. Sameness, proof, and emptiness are the wrong readings.

lessons.title: The emotional whole
lessons.objective: Assemble the full definition: an emotional appraisal that is pre-conceptual and aimed at both man and existence.

exercises.prompt: Calling the appraisal emotional means that it is

choices.text: Felt as an estimate of man and of existence
Infallible about the facts
A replacement for all thinking
A feeling with no object

feedback.note: Emotional names how the appraisal is held. It does not make the feeling infallible, a substitute for thought, or objectless.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the full definition.

pairs.right: A judgment, not a blank mood

feedback.note: The full definition needs form, timing, objects, and the fact that it judges. Leave one out and the phrase is no longer this unit.

exercises.prompt: Build the full definition.

feedback.note: Stop at the definition. A sense of life is not a substitute for thought added onto that sentence.

exercises.prompt: Contrast the emotional appraisal with a proof.

feedback.note: An emotional appraisal is felt. It is not proved, voted into place, or passed down as an inheritance.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a sense of life?

choices.text: An unstated emotional estimate that people can live successfully in the world
A reasoned essay that defines its terms and gives arguments
Annoyance at the price of one ticket
A list of facts with no judgment of man or existence

feedback.note: Only the unstated emotional estimate of man and existence matches the definition. An essay, a price, and a bare list do not.

exercises.prompt: Match each stand-in to the piece of the definition it misses.

pairs.left: A passing mood about one event
pairs.right: Misses man and existence as the objects

pairs.left: A feeling used as a proof
pairs.right: Misses that emotional does not mean cognitive

feedback.note: Each stand-in drops a different part of the definition: the objects, the timing, or the limit of emotion.

exercises.prompt: Which set of words is the whole definition?

choices.text: Pre-conceptual, emotional appraisal of man and of existence
Emotional, and nothing further
An appraisal of man only
Whatever one feels before breakfast

feedback.note: The unit’s definition needs every part. Emotion alone, man alone, or a morning mood is not the whole.

exercises.prompt: Restate the definition.

parts.text: A sense of life is a
appraisal of man and of existence.

feedback.note: The two adjectives are pre-conceptual and emotional. Arbitrary and scientific are not names for a sense of life.
